claim.why_it_matters: The '(combining)' qualifier of the Khmer and Mongolian combining-mark rows is detached from the row and left as a stray paragraph, so each script shows two identically-labelled rows and the combining marks read as letters.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (2014 p.768, PDF p792) shows the labels 'Khmer:' and 'Mongolian:' with '(combining)' wrapped onto a second line of the label cell, beside 17B4-17D3 and 18A9. The markdown keeps every code range in the correct row and puts '(combining)' on the line right after each of those rows, before the next row. So the qualifier is present and next to its row. The only difference is that a wrapped two-line label cell was split by table conversion. No code point, range or row assignment changes, and both sources list the same repertoire. This is a layout and wrapping artifact. It is not a content discrepancy.
